excerpt: DEFA14A 1 d136896ddefa14a.htm DEFA14A DEFA14A UNITED STATES SECURITIES AND EXCHANGE COMMISSION Washington, D.C. 20549 SCHEDULE 14A Proxy Statement Pursuant to Section 14(a) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (Amendment No.) Filed by the Registrant ☒ Filed by a Party other than the Registrant ☐ Check the appropriate box: ☐ Preliminary Proxy Statement ☐ Confidential, for Use of the Commission Only (as permitted by Rule 14a-6(e)(2)) ☐ Definitive Proxy Statement ☒ Definitive Additional Materials ☐ Soliciting Material under §240.14a-12 Microsoft Corporation (Name of Registrant as Specified In Its Charter) (Name of Person(s) Filing Proxy Statement, if other than the Registrant) Payment of Filing Fee (Check all boxes that apply): ☒ No fee required ☐ Fee paid previously with preliminary materials ☐ Fee computed on table in exhibit required by Item 25(b) per Exchange Act Rules 14a-6(i)(1) and 0-11 Supplement to the Proxy Statement for the 2026 Annual Shareholders Meeting of Microsoft Corporation to be held on December 8, 2026 This proxy statement supplement (“Supplement”), dated November 9, 2026, provides updated information with respect to the 2026 Annual Shareholders Meeting (“Annual Meeting”) of Microsoft Corporation (“Company”) to be held on December 8, 2026, beginning at 8:30 a.m. Pacific Time. This Supplement is being filed with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (“SEC”) and is being made available to the shareholders of the Company on or about November 9, 2026. Except as described in this Supplement, the information provided in the definitive proxy statement filed by the Company with the SEC on October 21, 2026 (“Proxy Statement”) continues to apply. To the extent the information in this Supplement differs from or updates information in the Proxy Statement, shareholders should rely on the information contained in this Supplement. You should read the entire Proxy Statement, this Supplement (which contains information that supplements and updates the Proxy Statement), and any additional proxy materials carefully before voting your shares. Withdrawal of director nominee As described in our Current Report on Form 8-K filed with the SEC on November 5, 2026, Emma N. Walmsley, a nominee for re-election as director, informed the Company’s Board of Directors of her decision to not stand for re-election at the Annual Meeting. As a result, Ms. Walmsley is no longer a director nominee for election at the Annual Meeting. Ms. Walmsley’s decision not to stand for re-election was not due to any disagreement with the Company on any matter relating to the Company’s operations, policies, or practices. In connection with Ms. Walmsley’s decision not to stand for re-election, the Board of Directors will be reduced to 11 members, effective as of the date of the Annual Meeting. Taking into account Ms. Walmsley’s decision not to stand for re-election, the following reflects demographic information about our 11 director nominees for election at the Annual Meeting: • 10 of 11 director nominees are independent; • the average tenure of director nominees is 6.8 years; • the average age of director nominees is 59; and • four of the director nominees are women. Voting matters If you have already returned your proxy or provided voting instructions, you do not need to take any action unless you wish to change your vote. Any proxies or voting instructions for or against Ms. Walmsley’s election will not be counted. Previously submitted proxies and voting instructions will remain valid with respect to all other director nominees and matters to be considered at the Annual Meeting. If you have not yet returned your proxy card or submitted your voting instructions, please complete and return the proxy card or submit voting instructions, disregarding Ms. Walmsley’s name as a director nominee. At the Annual Meeting, shareholders will vote on the election of the 11 remaining director nominees. No vacancy will result from Ms. Walmsley’s departure. None of the other items to be acted upon at the Annual Meeting, which are described in the Proxy Statement, are affected by this Supplement. The shares represented by proxy cards or voting instructions submitted before the Annual Meeting will be voted with respect to all other matters properly brought before the Annual Meeting as instructed on the proxy card or pursuant to the voting instructions. Information about how to vote your shares is available in the Proxy Statement. By Order of the Board of Directors Brian DeFoe Secretary November 9, 2026 Important Notice Regarding the Availability of Proxy Materials for the Shareholders Meeting to be held on December 8, 2026: Our Proxy Statement and 2026 Annual Report are available at www.proxyvote.com . This Supplement is being made available online at the same location on or about November 9, 2026.

Amin Vahdat SVP and Chief Technologist, AI and Infrastructure Share x.com Facebook LinkedIn Mail Copy link Read AI-generated summary We’re expanding our eighth-generation TPU portfolio with the new TPU 8tx for secure, confidential inference and TPU 8i Max for massive context windows. These systems help you manage complex agentic workloads by providing specialized hardware for security, density, and reasoning. You can learn more about these additions and our latest software updates by watching our broadcast or visiting the Google Cloud website to explore our full infrastructure lineup. Summaries were generated by Google AI. Generative AI is experimental. We are expanding our eighth-generation TPU portfolio with the new TPU 8tx and TPU 8i Max systems. TPU 8tx provides hardware-level security for sensitive data, while TPU 8i Max handles massive context windows. These systems join TPU 8t and TPU 8i to offer specialized performance for every AI lifecycle stage. We are making TPUs more accessible by supporting PyTorch, open-source software, and automated tools for developers. Summaries were generated by Google AI. Generative AI is experimental. Explore other styles: General summary Bullet points We first designed TPUs more than a decade ago motivated by Google’s internal demands, including voice recognition and language translation. Eight generations of TPUs later, the use cases have exploded, covering: i) training and serving our own Gemini models, ii) agentic workloads, iii) delivering services to Google Cloud customers on our cloud infrastructure, and most recently, iv) allowing customers to deploy TPUs directly into their own data centers. TPUs are now a rapidly growing business with nearly 100 customers — including frontier labs, trading firms, retailers, universities, and more. At Google Cloud Next in April, we introduced two new specialized TPUs in the same generation — 8t for large-scale training and 8i for real-time reasoning. TPU 8t and 8i offer up to 2.7 times better training performance and 80% better inference price performance, respectively, versus our previous generation of TPUs. Today, we’re taking that a step further, expanding our eighth-generation TPU portfolio with two additional systems: TPU 8i Max for massive context windows and the highest compute density per rack, and TPU 8tx for secure and confidential inference. This is the first time we have introduced four TPU systems in a single year. Our expanded eighth-generation TPU portfolio: TPU 8t, TPU 8i, TPU 8tx, and TPU 8i Max. While we’ve always co-designed our TPUs in partnership with Google DeepMind, we’re now increasingly getting feedback from external organizations on their specific needs. With computing moving from human to agent scale, businesses are asking for accelerators that can reason across AI models’ massive context windows. In addition, some highly regulated customers are asking for specialized encryption capabilities for unique workloads. The new TPU systems we are announcing today address this new reality.
